page: The UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-4xCPU-16GB is a general-purpose virtual server belonging to the Cloud Native family, running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with 4 vCPUs and 4 physical cores. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz with a shared allocation model. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, providing 4.0 GB of memory per core. It does not include any local storage or GPU hardware, but comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates moderate performance across standard workloads. The server achieves average results in Passmark CPU tests, including the CPU score of 7941.3, extended instructions, encryption, and physics tests. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also perform within the average range. However, the shared CPU allocation leads to lower performance in compute-intensive tasks, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core benchmarks scoring in the bottom 10% and 25% respectively. Memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks is weak, and write speeds are poor at 14.27 GB/sec.

Given the shared CPU allocation and lack of local storage, this server is positioned as a cost-efficient option for workloads that do not require sustained high-performance compute or high-speed disk I/O. It is suitable for basic web serving, lightweight database operations, and small-scale application hosting. It can also handle light text processing and small-model LLM inference, though performance drops significantly on larger models.
